targets.approach: Walk the Tahquitz north face trail, then go on toward Indian Buttress along faint paths that hug the creek. Once you are almost beneath Indian Buttress, cross the creek and climb the ravine to the foot of the Amphitheater itself, at the right-hand end of the First Terrace. The cirque as a whole is reached by way of the Strawberry Creek drainage. The route starts in a chimney and layback section that leads to a big pine tree.
targets.descent_text: From the top of the last pitch, hike down to the Devil's Slide trail, which returns to Humber Park.
targets.name: Crooked piton

targets.approach: The usual way in begins at Whitney Portal, climbs along the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek beside Iceberg Lake, goes over the Whitney-Russell col, and descends a small valley toward Guitar Lake. The south-facing wall sits just below and west of Arctic Lake. An alternative goes over Trail Crest on the Mt. Whitney Trail and down to Guitar Lake, which is more trail but more distance and gain. Camping is good at the west end of Arctic Lake, and from camp the wall is a day trip. The route is on the right side of the left-hand of the two formations above Arctic Lakes and begins on orange, featured rock.
targets.descent_text: Travel west from the summit, then turn south and descend back to the lakes.
targets.name: Chillin The Most

targets.approach: The usual way in begins at Whitney Portal, climbs along the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek beside Iceberg Lake, goes over the Whitney-Russell col, and descends a small valley toward Guitar Lake. The south-facing wall sits just below and west of Arctic Lake. An alternative goes over Trail Crest on the Mt. Whitney Trail and down to Guitar Lake, which is more trail but more distance and gain. Camping is good at the west end of Arctic Lake, and from camp the wall is a day trip. To find the start, look for the largest double-roof feature on the wall, then follow the single vertical crack at the left edge of those roofs down to the ground. The route starts in a flaky corner system there.
targets.descent_text: Walk off to the left from the top and follow the sandy slope back down.
targets.name: Cooler Than a Polar Bear's Toenails

targets.approach: The usual way in begins at Whitney Portal, climbs along the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek beside Iceberg Lake, goes over the Whitney-Russell col, and descends a small valley toward Guitar Lake. The south-facing wall sits just below and west of Arctic Lake. An alternative goes over Trail Crest on the Mt. Whitney Trail and down to Guitar Lake, which is more trail but more distance and gain. Camping is good at the west end of Arctic Lake, and from camp the wall is a day trip. The route starts at a distinct orange corner, to the right of the West Arete route, and takes a direct line toward the western summit of the formation.
targets.descent_text: Descend by the gentle slopes along the west ridge.
targets.name: Polar Express

targets.approach: The usual way in begins at Whitney Portal, climbs along the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek beside Iceberg Lake, goes over the Whitney-Russell col, and descends a small valley toward Guitar Lake. The south-facing wall sits just below and west of Arctic Lake. An alternative goes over Trail Crest on the Mt. Whitney Trail and down to Guitar Lake, which is more trail but more distance and gain. Camping is good at the west end of Arctic Lake, and from camp the wall is a day trip. This route is not on the main wall. It is on a smaller wall just above the lower camp below Arctic Lake Wall. Find the second large boulder to the right of a black streak; a clean crack splits the face above, with a stem-box chimney in the middle.
targets.descent_text: Walk off to the right from the top.
targets.name: Small Everything Blizzard

targets.approach: Bat Rock is a crag on the north side of Highway 155, west of Wofford Heights, and the hike up to it is steep. The route starts at the base of the far right side of the south face, at a natural mineral stain shaped like the Roman numeral nine.
targets.name: "IX"

targets.approach: The Bear's Behind is a south-facing wall a short, easy hike northwest of The Egg. Hairy Bear starts in the center of the south face, climbs the face to a right-slanting crack, and joins the route Sunkiss near the top.
targets.name: Hairy Bear

targets.approach: Take the trail from Lake Sabrina to Blue Lake, then expect a stretch of bushwhacking and scrambling to reach the crag on the south side of the lake. The dihedral is on the south side of Blue Lake.
targets.name: Blue Lake Dihedral

targets.approach: Take the trail from Lake Sabrina to Blue Lake, then expect a stretch of bushwhacking and scrambling to reach the crag on the south side of the lake. The crack is on the southeast side of the lake: weave through the boulder tier a level above the water until a hidden grassy meadow opens up. The crack is obvious from there.
targets.name: Shire Crack

targets.approach: Leave the car at the pack station where the Pine Creek road ends and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail. The Brownstone wall appears on the left, right beside the trail, so no off-trail travel is needed. The route is the obvious overhanging crack and dihedral to the left of the tree of the day.
targets.name: Bring the Bacon

targets.approach: Leave the car at the pack station where the Pine Creek road ends and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail. The Brownstone wall appears on the left, right beside the trail, so no off-trail travel is needed. Crystal Licker starts from a small block that lets you reach the first holds, and climbs through underclings to a crystal band.
targets.name: Crystal Licker

targets.approach: Leave the car at the pack station where the Pine Creek road ends and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail. The Brownstone wall appears on the left, right beside the trail, so no off-trail travel is needed. Enemy Mine is on the right side of the buttress, where grey bolts mark an arching flake that faces left and is climbed by laybacking.
targets.name: Enemy Mine

targets.approach: Leave the car at the pack station where the Pine Creek road ends and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail. The Brownstone wall appears on the left, right beside the trail, so no off-trail travel is needed. The route starts just off the trail. The variation start begins up the bolted route immediately to its left, then cuts right to a stance below the anchor of Mine's Eye.
targets.name: Mine In The Sky

targets.approach: Leave the car at the pack station where the Pine Creek road ends and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail. The Brownstone wall appears on the left, right beside the trail, so no off-trail travel is needed. Mine Over Matter lies a little higher on the slope than the Mine in the Sky start. A built-up platform marks the foot of a finger crack that leads into a bolted face.
targets.name: Mine Over Matter

targets.approach: Leave the car at the pack station where the Pine Creek road ends and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail. The Brownstone wall appears on the left, right beside the trail, so no off-trail travel is needed. Never Mined starts at a wide crack just to the right of Mine Over Matter.
targets.name: Never Mined

targets.approach: Leave the car at the pack station where the Pine Creek road ends and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail. The Brownstone wall appears on the left, right beside the trail, so no off-trail travel is needed. Nutter Butter starts a little right of the Mine in the Sky variation start and shares its first two bolts with I Me Mine.
targets.descent_text: Lower from the anchor hardware at the top.
targets.name: Nutter Butter

targets.approach: From Road's End in Kings Canyon, hike east on the trail to the good camp just past Charlotte Creek. From camp, continue a short distance to a climbers' trail and follow the cairns up into a steep dry streambed. Near its top, bear left into the main gully that ends the right side of the whole wall. The route climbs the first few pitches of Ikigai before splitting off toward the golden headwall.
targets.name: The Ecstasy of Gold

targets.approach: From the circular parking area, walk west and slightly uphill for a short hike to the formation. The route climbs a thin crack to a ledge on the right side of the main face, then the featured face above, to a bolted anchor.
targets.name: Hollow Point

targets.approach: Burnt Granola is the squarish cliff just north of where Highway 178 meets Chimney Peak Road. Park where Chimney Peak Road heads east under the cliff and walk a short way to the base. The route follows the center of the face to two obvious water cracks.
targets.name: Burnt Granola

targets.approach: The pinnacles are roadside, midway between Low Maintenance Rock and High Profile Pinnacle, north of Forest Road 2N13. Park along the road and walk a short distance north. The route is a hand-sized crack splitting the south face of the left pinnacle.
targets.name: Lover's Leap

targets.approach: The pinnacles are roadside, midway between Low Maintenance Rock and High Profile Pinnacle, north of Forest Road 2N13. Park along the road and walk a short distance north. The route follows a hand crack on the east face of the right pinnacle.
targets.name: Rollerblade

targets.approach: Head up the John Muir Trail toward Cathedral Lakes. After the second set of switchbacks, when the tip of the wall first shows, keep walking until the trail crosses the creek and climbs another set of switchbacks, then leave the trail and walk cross-country straight at the wall; the going is open, with no thick brush. The route is a direct line toward the top of the wall, and the corner that dominates the fourth pitch is the feature to aim for.
targets.name: The Direct Line

targets.approach: From the South Lake trailhead, take the Bishop Pass trail to Le Conte Canyon and turn south on the John Muir Trail along the Middle Fork of the Kings River for a couple of miles. Find a crossing of the river above the mouth of Ladder Creek, then work up the small side valley toward the Citadel, getting over Ladder Creek where it is easy. The east arete is the long east-facing ridge. To find the start, watch for a clean corner facing left, low on the ridge by the final bushes and trees.
targets.name: East Arete

targets.approach: Turn east off Highway 38 onto Forest Road 1N02, passing Heart Bar Campground and the two equestrian camps, and bear left at the Y. Continue along 1N02 until the rock comes into view beside the road on the right. Coondoggolin splits the middle of the south face by its prominent crack.
targets.name: Coondoggolin

targets.approach: Turn east off Highway 38 onto Forest Road 1N02, passing Heart Bar Campground and the two equestrian camps, and bear left at the Y. Continue along 1N02 until the rock comes into view beside the road on the right. Coonstock is on the left side of the south face; it crosses a few horizontal cracks on face holds before entering a widening crack that leans right.
targets.name: Coonstock

targets.approach: Turn east off Highway 38 onto Forest Road 1N02, passing Heart Bar Campground and the two equestrian camps, and bear left at the Y. Continue along 1N02 until the rock comes into view beside the road on the right. Racoon sits at the right end of the east face; face moves lead to a crack that opens up slowly.
targets.name: Racoon

targets.approach: Turn east off Highway 38 onto Forest Road 1N02, passing Heart Bar Campground and the two equestrian camps, and bear left at the Y. Continue along 1N02 until the rock comes into view beside the road on the right. Star Gazers is on the right side of the south face, going past horizontal cracks and flakes.
targets.name: Star Gazers

targets.approach: The formation is visible from Tioga Road near the Porcupine Creek trailhead. There is no trail: park at a pullout on either side of the formation (the one just east works a little better) and find your own way across the ground to the rocks. Acme Crack takes the southwest arete of the southernmost formation.
targets.name: Acme Crack

targets.approach: The formation is visible from Tioga Road near the Porcupine Creek trailhead. There is no trail: park at a pullout on either side of the formation (the one just east works a little better) and find your own way across the ground to the rocks. Dorada climbs the northeast arete of the southernmost feature, starting from a small podium near two bolts.
targets.name: Dorada

targets.approach: The formation is visible from Tioga Road near the Porcupine Creek trailhead. There is no trail: park at a pullout on either side of the formation (the one just east works a little better) and find your own way across the ground to the rocks. Pleasant View Arete follows the southwest arete of the southern formation.
targets.name: Pleasant View Arete

targets.approach: The formation is visible from Tioga Road near the Porcupine Creek trailhead. There is no trail: park at a pullout on either side of the formation (the one just east works a little better) and find your own way across the ground to the rocks. The route starts in the notch between the two formations, around the corner and up-left of Cattlestar Faticus, reached by easy class 2 ground with minimal brush, and climbs the southwest face of the higher formation.
targets.name: Upper Wall from Notch

targets.approach: Natural Resources Rock lies directly southwest of High Profile Pinnacle and very close to the road. Jungle Fever starts a few steps left of Natural Resources, up a lieback crack.
targets.name: Jungle Fever

targets.approach: Natural Resources Rock lies directly southwest of High Profile Pinnacle and very close to the road. Walk around behind the formation from the road and descend to roughly beneath the summit block. Start in the middle of the west face, on the first inviting crack just left of the summit.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the anchor on top of the summit block.
targets.name: Natural Resources

targets.approach: Park at the hairpin turn; the trail heads north from the bend. It crests a small rise, drops to cross a seasonal stream, then switchbacks uphill to The Coven at the base of Dragonlance Wall, the first wall reached. Dobby's Dungeon starts behind a large pine, left of Squeal Like A Pig and close to the right of the gully used to reach Voodoo Wall.
targets.name: Dobby's Dungeon

targets.approach: From Emerald Bay, take the trail to Eagle Lake and get across its outlet. Work along the lakeshore, then swing up and to the right toward the foot of a big gully full of talus, whose right side is a tall rock wall. Climb the gully until it flattens into a benched area with views of the Velma Lakes, cross the bench while keeping the buttress in sight, and where the bench bends away, weave up the slabs on the right to an obvious ridge that leads to the base. This route is on the small crag at the foot of the northeast face of Eagle Lake Buttress. It climbs the blunt southeast arete; look for the right-leaning splitter crack with a small left-facing offset.
targets.descent_text: Build a gear anchor at the top and walk off.
targets.name: Purple Flame

targets.approach: From Emerald Bay, take the trail to Eagle Lake and get across its outlet. Work along the lakeshore, then swing up and to the right toward the foot of a big gully full of talus, whose right side is a tall rock wall. Climb the gully until it flattens into a benched area with views of the Velma Lakes, cross the bench while keeping the buttress in sight, and where the bench bends away, weave up the slabs on the right to an obvious ridge that leads to the base. This route is on the small crag at the foot of the northeast face of Eagle Lake Buttress. It takes the zigzag crack in the center of the east face, which is identified by a clear horizontal crack low on the face.
targets.descent_text: Build a gear anchor on the nuts or cams at the top and walk off.
targets.name: Slash and Burn

targets.approach: Leave the car beside the road above the Wilderness Permit Center, or use that center's lot. Begin just east of the turnoff to the permit center and Tuolumne Lodge and head north, uphill; a good trail begins a short way in but can be hard to spot the first time. The wall is east-facing and the first climbs come up after a short uphill walk, with the far end a little farther on. Alive at Leads climbs broken flakes to a single bolt on the slab above.
targets.name: Alive at Leads

targets.approach: Leave the car beside the road above the Wilderness Permit Center, or use that center's lot. Begin just east of the turnoff to the permit center and Tuolumne Lodge and head north, uphill; a good trail begins a short way in but can be hard to spot the first time. The wall is east-facing and the first climbs come up after a short uphill walk, with the far end a little farther on. Big Dog Hammer is left of Dos Equis and climbs knobs past two bolts.
targets.name: Big Dog Hammer

targets.approach: Leave the car beside the road above the Wilderness Permit Center, or use that center's lot. Begin just east of the turnoff to the permit center and Tuolumne Lodge and head north, uphill; a good trail begins a short way in but can be hard to spot the first time. The wall is east-facing and the first climbs come up after a short uphill walk, with the far end a little farther on. Dos Equis is left of Middle of the Road and climbs knobs past two bolts.
targets.name: Dos Equis

targets.approach: Leave the car beside the road above the Wilderness Permit Center, or use that center's lot. Begin just east of the turnoff to the permit center and Tuolumne Lodge and head north, uphill; a good trail begins a short way in but can be hard to spot the first time. The wall is east-facing and the first climbs come up after a short uphill walk, with the far end a little farther on. Elephant's Massacre is right of Shots a' Gold and wanders up slab and a bulge.
targets.name: Elephant's Massacre
